title: 多模态数据融合视角下江南古典园林美学特征量化建模研究
visual_status: ORIGINAL 116-PAGE PDF ALL-PAGE VISUAL AUDIT; printed code pp86-116 audited

problem_data_contract.independent_evaluation_unit: Q1 garden/route candidate; Q2 garden and expert/measurement validation point; Q3 garden for unseen-garden generalization, with pairwise labels nested within garden entities
problem_data_contract.input_structure: 10 core Jiangnan gardens with vector geometry; Q3 claims additional image/text modalities and 10 new gardens; appendix prints partial Python source but does not provide a complete runnable project/data bundle
problem_data_contract.validation_priority: split/hold out at garden/entity level before creating pairwise examples; separate constructed score calibration from expert validation; require deterministic feature provenance; require method-defining code primitives before treating printed outputs as reproduction evidence
problem_data_contract.author_evaluation_scope: within-sample route/score analyses, expert correlations, constructed validation metrics, 5-fold claims and additional-garden visualizations; several printed-code paths use placeholders/fixed outputs

questions.Q1: weighted undirected route graph -> curvature/turning/crossing descriptors + field-of-view landscape-change score -> interest utility -> claimed improved-GA route optimization and Pareto comparison
questions.Q2: element area/shape/distribution + open-close sequence descriptors -> AHP-entropy combination -> illusion score/ranking -> MRE/Kappa/coherence/ARI/CV-MSE validation
questions.Q3: geometry/image/text multimodal extraction -> MKL + contrastive embedding -> feature/topology/behavior similarities -> claimed unseen-garden validation; extended perspective aesthetics adds ray/geometry scores plus NeRF/STGCN/multitask regularization

evidence: printed Python appendix pp86-116 static audit
not_achieved: R3: printed code is incomplete and materially drifts from the paper; no original-data smoke test of a self-contained chain
R4-R7: no partial/full original-data reproduction, independent implementation or transfer attributable to S044

key_strengths: Q1 preserves a useful transparent chain from walkable graph and scene-change descriptors to route utility, and explicitly frames interest vs repeated distance as competing objectives.
Q2 decomposes illusion into interpretable element-distribution and open-close dynamics rather than relying only on a black-box score.
Q3 correctly recognizes that geometric, visual and semantic evidence are conceptually distinct modalities and that pairwise similarity should be validated against external preference/labels.
The paper contains extensive diagrams, maps, heatmaps and a long printed appendix, enabling unusually strong static paper-code auditing even though execution is incomplete.
key_risks: Q1 paper advertises improved-GA/Pareto optimization, but the printed route-planning function only computes one Dijkstra shortest path; the algorithm-defining primitive is absent from code evidence.

Q1 Eq.(17) converts the advertised two-objective problem to one weighted scalar fitness; a single utility operating point must not be presented as a preserved Pareto set without a separate nondominated mechanism.

Q1 route-map/convergence figures show search behavior, not certified optimality; expert-correlation and MANOVA/t-test sections require actual statistics/sample-unit provenance, not method descriptions alone.
Q2 code injects stochastic surrogate fractal/NNI/openness/contag features under a real-data pipeline and finally replaces computed scores with fixed ranking dictionaries.
Q2 paper says AHP-entropy while printed code labels AHP-CRITIC and hard-codes weights, so the weighting method has paper-code semantic drift.
Q2 Table 15 uses criterion Kappa>0.833 while reporting Kappa=0.833; the stated strict threshold is not satisfied by the displayed value.
Q2 validation values MRE/Kappa/coherence/ARI/CV-MSE are not visibly generated by the printed Q2 code, and the final score uncertainties in Table 13 are not produced by the fixed-score dictionary.
Q3 p-value provenance drifts: prose assigns Pearson p=0.012 and Spearman p=0.018, whereas Table 17 pairs Pearson with p=0.018 and Spearman with p=0.012.

Q3 claims multimodal MKL + deep metric learning + persistence-homology + HMM, but printed code has stubbed data extraction, empty feature assembly, omitted training and an untrained embedding network; topology/behavior scores are relabeled distances from that same embedding.

Q3 if pairwise contrastive examples from only ten gardens are randomly split by pair, the same garden can occur in train and validation; unseen-garden claims require group/entity split, but the visible protocol does not establish it.

Q3 perspective validation code clamps R2 to [0.75,0.95] and hard-codes 5-fold MSE/MAE/R2=30.0/4.5/0.78, exactly matching Table 19 generalization values; these cannot serve as computed validation evidence.
Q3 visualizations such as t-SNE clusters and similarity heatmaps are descriptive; bright diagonal/self-similarity is mathematical identity, not evidence of external validity or generalization.
recommended_redo: Q1 keep graph/visibility/scene-change descriptors, but use k-shortest/beam/label-setting or a genuine nondominated archive; choose GA only if the candidate graph is too large and verify that printed/executable code actually implements its genetic primitives.

Q2 remove all synthetic/random stand-ins from the production feature path, compute AHP and entropy/CRITIC weights from auditable sources, freeze normalization on a calibration cohort, and validate against independent expert/measurement data.

Q3 begin with compact deterministic geometric features plus pretrained image/text embeddings only when those modalities truly exist; use garden-level holdout before pair construction; promote contrastive/MKL/PH/HMM only with sufficient independent gardens and executable primitives.
For the perspective extension, use a transparent deterministic ray/visibility score as the baseline; promote NeRF/STGCN only with real image/view/time data and held-out evaluation.
Generate every headline metric/ranking from one Result Registry; never clip metrics or hard-code cross-validation outputs.
